text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) Issue Department foreign currency assets fell by 51 million marks to 3.478 billion marks in the week to August 15, the BNB said.
-- Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant said it had shut down its first reactor because of technical problems. No radiation polution was reported. @
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had sold 25.4 percent of Sofia-based plastic packaging producer Sofiaplast to Sofiaplast's employees for $1.5 million.

-- Bulgarian customs officers at the Bulgarian-Turkish border checkpoint of Kapitan Andreevo said they had seized 226 kilogrammes of silver hidden in a Turkish truck transiting from Romania to Turkey. @

-- Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) which manages state equity on commercial banks had extended the deadline for receiving bids for a stake in Varna-based Expressbank by two weeks to September 3, BCC executive director Petar Zhotev said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet may revoke the sale of a 75 percent stake in Bulgaria's second biggest oil refinery Plama to Bulgaria's Euroenergy Holding due to Plama's outstanding debts to creditors amonting to around 150 billion levs and 5.4 billion lev debt to the state, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said. Plama was sold last year for 62 million levs. @
-- Bulgaria's cabinet set a working group which should submit projects for new identification documents of Bulgarians due to be introduced next year, the government presscentre said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to complete next year the preparation for the sale of Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved the spending of 63.1 billion levs from the state fund Zemedelie this year to support agricultural production, the government presscentre said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
